results.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
results.proof_sketch: For every graph G, a set C is a vertex cover exactly when V(G)\C is independent. Hence τ(G)=n−α(G), and τ(G)≤k exactly when G has an independent m-set. Complementation turns independent m-sets into K_m subgraphs, proving the identity. For k=1, every admissible edge set is a subset of one of the n labelled stars. The empty graph is counted once; a one-edge graph is counted twice in the star sum; and any admissible graph with at least two edges has a unique common center. This gives the displayed formula. The remaining endpoint formulas follow immediately from requiring independent sets of sizes two or one.

results.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
results.proof_sketch: For every k-subset C⊆[n], generate the 2^q graphs having no edge inside [n]\C. For each generated graph, inspect all k-subsets preceding C in a fixed lexicographic order and count the graph only if none is a vertex cover. Every graph with τ≤k has a k-element cover, obtained by extending any smaller cover, and it is generated and retained exactly for its first k-cover. There are binom(n,k)2^q generated pairs, and the canonicality test uses at most binom(n,k) polynomial-time cover tests. Thus the time is poly(n)·binom(n,k)^2·2^q=2^{q+O(n)}, with only the current graph and counters stored. If k=o(n), then q≤nk=o(n²).

results.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
results.proof_sketch: Count graphs of vertex-cover number exactly t by their lexicographically first minimum cover C. Fix C and H=G[C]. Write I=[n]\C; I must be independent, and each v∈I is described by its neighborhood type A_v⊆C. For every nonempty independent X⊆V(H), let U_X={v∈I:A_v∩X≠∅}. Replacing X in C by U_X gives a cover, so C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every such X. When equality holds, this is another minimum cover; C precedes it exactly when min X<min U_X. Scan I in label order. For each X, a dynamic-programming state stores |U_X| capped at |X|+1 and whether U_X contains a label below min X. Choosing one of 2^t neighborhood types updates every coordinate. The final conditions are |U_X|>|X|, or equality without a below-minimum label. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates and at most 2(t+2) values per coordinate. Summing over C and the 2^{binom(t,2)} choices of H yields the bound and counts every graph exactly once.

results.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
results.proof_sketch: For a graph G let X(G) be its number of independent m-subsets. Summing over a chosen m-set gives sum_G X(G)=S1. For an ordered pair S,T with |S∩T|=j, independence of both forces exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) edges to be absent. Counting such ordered pairs gives S2=sum_G X(G)^2. The upper bound follows from 1_{X>0}≤X. Cauchy–Schwarz gives S1²≤F·S2. Finally, fixing one particular independent m-set supplies 2^q distinct qualifying graphs. The logarithmic bracket uses binom(n,m)≤2^n.

results.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
results.proof_sketch: P_n counts pairs consisting of a bipartite graph and an ordered proper two-coloring: choose the first color class and then choose arbitrary cross edges. If C(x) is the exponential generating series for connected bipartite graphs, then uncolored bipartite graphs have series B(x)=exp(C(x)). Every connected bipartite graph has exactly two ordered proper two-colorings, including an isolated vertex, so the colored series is P(x)=exp(2C(x))=B(x)^2. Comparing degree-n coefficients yields the recurrence. Every bipartite graph is triangle-free, so B_n≤T(n,3), and the complement identity gives the stated bound.

final_writeup: The full uniform 2^{o(n²)} algorithm remains unresolved here. The main positive result is an exact 2^{kn−k(k+1)/2+O(n)} algorithm, which settles every asymptotic regime k=o(n), together with a polynomial-time algorithm for each fixed k. The uncovered range includes k=n−3, which is already equivalent to exact enumeration of labelled triangle-free graphs. The moment formulas and bipartite recurrence provide independently checkable bounds in that range but do not determine the exact count.
checks_performed: Exhaustively enumerated every labelled graph for each 1≤n≤6, totaling 33,867 graphs. The exact vertex-cover distributions obtained were [1,0], [1,1,0], [1,6,1,0], [1,22,40,1,0], [1,65,570,387,1,0], and [1,171,4970,21837,5788,1,0].
Verified on those instances the complement identity, canonical k-cover generation, all endpoint formulas, the lexicographic minimum-cover dynamic program, and the first/second-moment inequalities.
Verified the bipartite power-series recurrence against direct bipartiteness testing for every graph through n=6. All checks used Python exact integers and passed.
